newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FURYK LEADS PEBBLE BEACH PRO-AM AFTER SECOND-ROUND 65.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FURYK LEADS PEBBLE BEACH PRO-AM AFTER SECOND-ROUND 65.

text.p: Jim Furyk shot a seven-under-par 65 to take the second round lead at 12 under par in the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am on Friday.
Furyk's round at Poppy Hills G.C. left him a stroke ahead of South African David Frost, who shot a 63 at Pebble Beach G.L., one stroke shy of the course record set by Tom Kite in 1983.

Tied for third place at 10 under were Paul Stankowski, who played with Furyk at Poppy and shot a 67 and Mark O'Meara, the only four-time winner of this tournament. He shot his 67 at Spyglass Hill G.C..
Five players were at nine under par, including first-round co-leader Jesper Parnevik, who shot a 70 at Pebble Beach.

The three Monterey Peninsula courses, Pebble Beach, Spyglass Hill and Poppy Hills, are the venues for the first three rounds, which are played in a pro-am format of two-man teams. On Sunday the top 60 pros, and top 25 pro-am teams, play at host course Pebble Beach.
What makes this tournament special is not the good rounds by the pros, but the presence of celebrity amateurs.
The star pairing this week was Tiger Woods and actor Kevin Costner. Woods shot an even par round of 72 at Poppy Hills to finish at two under for the tournament, 10 strokes off the

Furyk started on Poppy's 511 yard 10th hole, ordinarily a reachable par five, but when Furyk came through it was covered in fog and he laid up with a five-iron, then hit a little wedge shot to the green he couldn't see land four feet from the hole. When Furyk was on the next hole play was suspended for 35 minutes until the fog cleared.
Furyk birdied the 10th, the first of seven birdies on Friday, though he missed three other birdie putts inside of eight feet.
Furyk has the most unusual swing on the PGA Tour, with a looping action David Feherty once described as looking like an octopus falling from a tree. He calls it a natural and athletic swing.

He kept his drives in the fairways and his irons on the greens, so Furyk benefitted minimally from the preferred lie rule in place this week because of the heavy rains that had saturated the courses this month.

Frost on the other hand, said that the lift, clean and place rule saved him at least two strokes on Friday. Said Frost, "obviously, whenever you can get the ball in your hand it helps, particularly in the rough."

Frost had nine birdies and was one of the few people not complaining about heel prints and spike marks on the greens. "Actually, I think this is the best I've ever seen the greens at Pebble," said Frost.

He added that the round was among the most memorable of his career. "I even kept my ball, which I never do. It's such a great and famous golf course, that to shoot such a good round is something really special." lead.
